checks: No eclipse at 1 of 9 covered epochs where the 5.62423 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 201317466 is an eclipsing binary star candidate with an orbital period of 5.6242 days. The primary eclipse causes a 12.09% dimming in brightness, detected with very high significance - a signal-to-noise ratio of 562.4 using automated analysis of TESS photometry. A secondary eclipse was also detected at 5.4 sigma significance, occurring near orbital phase 0.49, suggesting both stars in the system eclipse each other as seen from Earth. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 86.0, though the centroid offset of 2.0 arcsec from the target position warrants consideration. This candidate does not appear in any of six checked variable-star catalogs. The automated pipeline assigned it a machine-learning score of 0.82, indicating a high likelihood of being a genuine eclipsing binary.
